issues.description: Command names violate the codebase's own convention (singular noun, hyphen).
issues.detail: The existing siblings are quickmark_save, quickmark_load, quickmark_del, bookmark_add, bookmark_load. This patch adds quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload — plural and inconsistent. Match the file's voice: quickmark_reload, bookmark_reload. The feature tests reference :bookmarks-reload / :quickmarks-reload, so this is wrong in three places at once.

issues.description: Two commands in one patch — split it.
issues.detail: quickmarks reload and bookmarks reload are independent user-visible features touching different objreg targets. THREE-PATCHES, or at minimum two: one for the refactor extracting reload() on UrlMarkManager, then one per command. As submitted, bisecting a regression on either command points at a single noisy commit.

issues.description: Reload silently drops in-memory marks added since startup.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() and rereads the file. Any quickmark added via quickmark_add but not yet flushed to disk by the save-manager is gone. No warning, no confirmation prompt, no docstring caveat. At minimum document it; better, force a save first or refuse if dirty.

Every other Scenario in this file has a descriptive title; the two new ones are bare `Scenario:`. Trivial to fix and the surrounding file's voice demands it. Name them, e.g. `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks (:bookmark-reload)`.

issues.description: Unit test doesn't cover the clear-old-entries path.
issues.detail: test_reload replaces one URL with another and checks the new one is present. It never asserts the old http://example.com is gone — which is the whole point of clearing self.marks before reloading. Add an assertion, or write the test as add-then-remove-on-disk-then-reload.

issues.description: No doc/changelog entry for two new user-facing commands.
issues.detail: New :commands need an entry in doc/help/commands.asciidoc (or whatever generates it) and a changelog line. The patch ships user-visible surface area with no documentation. Maintainer-six-months-from-now will get the bug report and have to grep for it.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The refactor is fine — extracting reload() onto UrlMarkManager and reusing it from __init__ is good taste, eliminates a duplicated loop. But the command names are plural where the entire surrounding file is singular (quickmark_save, bookmark_add), which is a tone-deaf style violation against the codebase's own voice. This is also two features jammed into one diff and should be split. Bigger concern: reload() wipes in-memory state with no regard for unsaved additions and no warning in the docstring. Tests don't assert the old entry is actually gone, and the feature scenarios are unnamed. Fix the names, split the patch, document the destructive behavior, then resubmit.
